Indian Stand& SPECIFICATION FOR THERMOPLASTICS HOSES ( TEXTILE REINFORCED ) FOR COMPRESSED AIR 0.
0.1 This

FOREWORD
prescribes requirements, `methods of sampling and test for air hose of rubber suitable for working pressure up to 1'4 MPa. 0.4 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from IS0 5774-1980 ( E ) `Plastic hoses - Textile - Reinfoiced thermoplastics type for compressed air - Specification', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). 0.5 This standard contains clauses 4.1.3., 4.2.1 and 7.1 which call for an agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revfsed ).

Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 9 November 1988, after the draft finalized by the Rubber Products Sectional Committee had `been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and related Products Division Cotihcil. 0.2 Due to growing manufacture and usage of thermoplastics hoses in the developed countries, they are also being used in India and consequently some manufacturers have also started producing them. Depending upon the usage, both rubber and plastics houses have their comparative advantages and weak points. However, once the choice to use thermoplastic hose has been exercised, it is important to stipulate the parameters to be tested and also prescribe the most acceptable requirements. Taking cognizance of these changes and developments, it was decided to formulate a standard for thermoplastic hoses. 0.3 IS : 446-1987.
*Specification

has already

been formulated

for rubber air hose (&WA revislon ).

requirements, 1.1 This standard prescribes methods of sampling and test for thermoplastics hoses with textile reinforcement suitable for working pressure up to 1'4 Mpa and application in temperature range -10 to +55"C. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in various parts of IS : 7503* shall apply. 3. TYPES

air hose for heavy duty mining and construction work with a maximum pressure of 1'4 MPa.

4. REQUIREMENTS The hose shall be uniform in colour ( transparency ), opacity and other physical properties. 4.1.1 Lining - A flexible thermoplastics resistant to oil mist. 4.1.2 Reinforcement textile reinforcement. A natural lining

industrial air hoses with maximum working pressure of 0'7 MPa, b) Type 2 - indurtrial air hoses with a maximum working pressure of 1.O MPa, and of terms used in rubber industry. 1

4.1.3 Cover - A flexible thermoplastic cover which may have a smooth or fluted finish as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. The colour may be different from that of the lining.
NOTE- The cover and the lining shall be fully gelled and free from visible cracks, porosity, foreign inclusions or other defects which might affect serviceability.

4.2 Dimensions

and Tolerances

42.1 Bore Size - The Bore size when measured according to the method prescribed in 42J.2 of IS : 443- 1975* shall be as given in Table 1. Other sizes within this range may be supplied by agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. The tolerances for these shall be those applicable to previous smaller size. 4.2.2 Lining and Cover Thickness - The thickness of lining and the cover of the hoses when measured according to the method prescribed in 4.2.2 of IS : 443-1975* shall be not less than that specified in Table 1. 4.2.3 The tolerance be f 1 percent. on any hose length shall

with the method prescribed in IS : 3400 ( Part 5 )1986" the minimum adhesion value between the lining and the cover, shall not be less than 1'5 KN/m.
4.4.2 Pressure Requirements - When tested in accordance with the method prescribed in 8 of IS : 443-1975t, the hose shall comply with the requirements given in Table 2 and shall show no leakage, porosity or rupture.

4.3 Physical Requirements
4.3.1 Resistance to Liquids - The lining, when tested by the method prescribed in IS : 3400 ( Part 6 )-1983t, immersing in oil No. 1 for 70 f 2" at a temperature of 50f 1" shall not show a volume change greater than 15 percent.

4.4.3 Cold Bend Radius - The hose shall be subjected to a temperature of -10 f 3�C for 24 hours in a straight position. After this time and while still at - lO"C, the hose shall be evenly and uniformly bent over a mandrel having a diameter equal to twice the minimum bend radius specified in Table 3. Bending shall be accomplished within a period of not less than 8 seconds and not more than 12 seconds. Hoses of less than 25 mm nominal bore shall be bent through 180" over the mandrel, and hoses of 25 mm nominal bore and above shall be bent through 90" over the madrel. After bending, the hose shall be allowed to attain ( or return to ) ambient temperature and shall be visually examined for cover cracks, then subjected to the proof test described in IS : 443-l 975t at the appropriate value specified in Table 2. There shall be no cover cracks or leakage.

4.3.2 Loss in Mass of Heating - Samples of lining and cover, when tested in accordance with the method prescribed in Appendix A, shall not show a loss in mass greater than 4 percent. 4.4 Performance Requirements

A-4.1.4 Place the container in the oven or thermostatic bath controlled at a temperature of 100 f 1�C. Ad-I.5 After 24 h, remove the container from the bath or oven and allow it to cool at room temperature. Remove the specimens from the container, carefully brush them free from any trace of carbon particles and recondition under the same conditions as those to which they were subjected before the original weighing. A-4.1.6 Reweigh each specimen to the nearest 0.001 g. NOTE- For different materials, different temperature and duration of test may be agreed betweoa the iateresc ted parties, maintaining the same test precedure. A-5. EXPRESSION OF RESULTS

Containers - metal cans, of cylindrical from about 180 mm in diameter and 120 mm in height provided with non-air tight cover ; a lid with a small vent hole of 3 mm diameter may be suitable.

A-l.5 Cylindrical Metal Cages - constructed from bronze gauze having apertures of approximately 500 pm, with a diameter of 60 mm and a height of 6 mm, formed by soldering a strip of the gauze at right angles to the periphery of a disc of the gauze, a similar but slightly larger cylinder acts as a lid. A-1.6 Activated Carbon - with a grain size of about 4 to 6 mm, free from powder. The carbon shall be of a wall determined type and grade, in order to obtain concordant results. Before use, the carbon should be sieved and dried to constant mass at 7O"C, preferably under vacuum and then stored in an air tight container. Use fresh material for each test. A-2. TEST SPECIMENS A-2.1 The test specimens shall be annular rings with height of 5 mm cut from hose sample. A-2.2 At least three test specimens shall be tested for each material. A-3. CONDITIONING A-3.1 Test specimens shall be conditioned in an atmosphere with a temperature of 27 & 2�C and 65 h 5 percent relative huminity for 24 hours. A-4. PROCEDURE A-4.1 Test Specimen
in

The change in mass, A m, expressed as a percentage, is given by the formula: Am= m"-ml~x
m0

100

where me = mass, in grams, of the test specimen after conditioning; and m, = mass, in grams, of the test specimen after treatment in the oven or thermostatical bath and reconditioning.
NOTBI - The arithmetic mean of the values obtained from the three test specimens is the loss of plasticizers from the material under test.

A-6. TEST REPORT The report shall include the following particulars : a) Reference to this standard; b) Complete identification of the sample and the procedure used for preparing the specimens; c) Thickness of each test specimen, to the nearest 0'01 mm; Mass of each test specimen, in grams, d) before the test and the gain or loss in mass, in miligrams, during the test; e) Mass change of each test specimen, expressed as a percentage of the original mass; f) Arithmetic mean of the values obtained from the three test specimens; 8) Observations on any change in appearance of the test specimens; and h) Date of test.

Wire Cages

A-4.1.1 After conditioning, weigh each test specimen to the nearest 0'001 g and determine its mean thickness to the nearest 0'01 mm. A-4.1.2 On the bottom of a metal container, spread about 120 cm3 of activated carbon. Place twice test specimens into a small metal wire-mesh cage thus avoiding direct contact between the plastic and the carbon. Finally put the lid on the container. A-4.1.3 Only test specimen of same composition shall be placed in one container, in order to avoid the possibility of plasticizers or other components migrating from one specimen to another.
